EFFECTIVE_MODEL: [m:minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview (thinking) — requested MiniMax M3.1 Flash + thinkingEffort=xhigh, reused session choices, recovery attempt 2 of the same first-wave task after the provider 500 | runtimeMode=plan (Plan Mode active, read-only enforcement is instruction-based per brief) | interactionMode=plan | configured readbacks at /Users/corvette/.t3/userdata/skill-lens-repair-checkpoints/2026-10-15-stage-e-work/council-r1-readbacks.json were NOT re-verified against this task's actual spawn — upstream model identity, effort=xhigh application, and reviewer family diversity remain UNVERIFIED; no attestation invented]

VERDICT: pass

BLOCKERS: none.

Independent reproduction summary (all read-only; disposable copies under /tmp; nothing written into the checkout):

- Gates re-run and matched exactly: pytest 967 passed / 1 skipped / 90.53% ≥ 90 (skip is the pre-existing case-insensitive-FS case in tests/test_session_snapshot.py:1951); mypy clean, 36 files; ruff check clean; ruff format --check clean, 135 files; targeted Python 3.14 with `-W error::DeprecationWarning:skill_lens.tui` 37 passed; TUI/session/routing/snapshot suites 106 passed / 1 skipped.
- All 13 coordinator mutations independently re-derived from the recorded diffs and re-executed; every one killed with0/1/0. Both previously-surviving loop guards (`r03_retain_owned_loop`, `r03_restore_closed_prior`) were killed on **both** 3.11 and 3.14 by my own runs, confirming the P2/P3 correction. Recorded source SHA-256s match the live files exactly, and all 506 entries in `council-r1-before.json` are unchanged — no drift since the wave opened.
- Review question verified directly rather than by proxy: `get_event_loop()` restores the exact borrowed *non-running* loop on 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14; on 3.14 both the old and new forms raise `RuntimeError` when no loop is set, so control flow is unchanged and only the deprecation disappears — confirming R03 was a deprecation, not a crash. `get_running_loop()` alone was correctly rejected as insufficient. No `asyncio.run`/`Runner`, executor join, private internals, or global warning suppression. Prompt-quit proof and stale-callback tests still pass; no snapshot/golden, registry, render, model, exitcode, dependency, lock or CI change; `.path` preserved.

SUGGESTIONS:

1. `skill_lens/cli.py:471` — `except (KeyError, ValueError)` catches *any* `ValueError` from the compare pipeline, not just the intended self-comparison. Forced adversarially (`run_compare` raising `ValueError("unrelated internal detail")`) it exits 2 with a usage-style literal message, so a genuine internal bug would be reported as a user error. It stays safe (no traceback, empty stdout) and is asymmetric with `why`, which still catches only `KeyError`. Optional future narrowing to a dedicated validation exception type; not a Stage E defect.
2. 3.12/3.13 are in the CI matrix but no targeted R03 run was executed there. I probed the stdlib directly: behaviour is identical old-vs-new on both, including the same implicit-creation `DeprecationWarning` each form emits, so there is no regression — but adding 3.12/3.13 to the targeted run would give CI parity.

FILES_AT_RISK: [skill_lens/cli.py (F08 stream guard ordering; widened ValueError catch), skill_lens/core/compare.py (shared validator must precede discovery), skill_lens/core/snapshot.py (captured-service parity), skill_lens/tui/__init__.py (event-loop ownership/restoration), tests/test_stage_e_repairs.py (37 tests incl. 4 loop-ownership proofs), tests/test_tui_routing.py (superseded explicit-bypass test), tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_compare.py, tests/test_tui_app.py]

CONCEDED: [duplicate parametrized examples and the long test module are non-blocking; the disabled-reason cleanup is Stage D carry-over outside Stage E; the placeholder UI has no comparison selection screen, so adapter/service agreement is proven at the service boundary without building U7; the superseded explicit-TTY bypass test is authorized by F08; the initial coordinator3.14 `--no-cov` rejection was a harness mismatch (external env lacks pytest-cov), not a product failure; no full-Linux/full-3.14/unexecuted-CI claim is made]
